122  THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE

In the second place, a number of the Indian students were well fitted to receive and profit by the training of the College because of their family backgrounds. At least two of the students marked for achievement of noteworthy distinction were Smith and Will Paul, and two brothers—and Moses Chipley, of Davis, whose photograph and sketch appear by photograph in the introduction in Chapter I; the brief accounts of the Paul brothers and of Moses Chipley are quoted as follows:

Smith and Will Paul.—Smith Paul, who received his education at Paul's Valley, Texas, completing his literary course in the school at Paul's, and then afterwards a business course in Mahon's Business College in Dallas in the 1880's and after 1900 at McGee was the proprietor of the Weekly Enterprise, published at Paul's Valley. In addition to his life as a public publisher, he turned his talent as a public man towards farming and stock-raising interest, and to his talent as a public man. He also served as deputy collector, and in both his public and individual capacities he has carried well the commendation of all.

Mr. Paul was educated in the early school days at Paul's Valley. He is a member of the Modern Woodmen of America. He stands in his community as a man of good character, strong moral ability and sterling worth.
